Meccan; its verses are 3. «It was revealed after Surat al-Sharh.» In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

He swears by the 'Asr prayer (the afternoon prayer) because of its excellence, as is shown by His saying, the Exalted: "and the middle prayer," which in the codex (mushaf) of Hafsah is "the 'Asr prayer"; and by his saying, upon him be peace and blessings: "Whoever misses the 'Asr prayer, it is as if he has been robbed of his family and his property." [[Agreed upon, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both.]] Also because the obligation to perform it is harder, since people are pressed in their trade and earnings at the end of the day and busy with their livelihoods.

Or He swears by the afternoon (al-'ashiyy), just as He swore by the forenoon (al-duha), because both contain signs of His power. Or He swears by time, because of the various kinds of wonders in its passing. "Al-insan" (man) refers to the whole kind. "Al-khusr" is "al-khusran" (loss), just as it is said "al-kufr" for "al-kufran" (ingratitude). The meaning is: people are in loss in their trading, except the righteous alone, because they bought the Hereafter with this world, so they profited and were made happy; while the others traded in the opposite way, so they fell into loss and misery. ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾ means the firmly established matter whose denial cannot be allowed, which is all good: affirming God's oneness and obeying Him, following His books and messengers, being detached from this world, and desiring the Hereafter. ﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾ means patience in refraining from acts of disobedience, in persevering in acts of obedience, and in what God tests His servants with.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat Wa'l-'Asr, God will forgive him, and he will be among those who enjoined one another to the truth and enjoined one another to patience." [[Narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with a chain going back to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]]
